walkthroughs.body_html:
Elizabeth became queen in November 1558, aged 25.

She was unmarried, Protestant, and had survived prison under her Catholic sister Mary I. England was bankrupt, divided over religion, and threatened by Catholic France and Spain.

In 1559 Elizabeth chose a 'middle way'.

The Act of Supremacy made her Supreme Governor — a careful word, since Catholics disliked a female 'head' of the Church. The Act of Uniformity set one Protestant prayer book but kept some traditional ceremonies.

Elizabeth ruled with her Privy Council — around 19 trusted advisors.

William Cecil (Lord Burghley) served her for 40 years. Parliament was called only when she needed money or new laws. She rarely visited the north or far west, ruling through lords and JPs.

mcqs.q: What was the Elizabethan Religious Settlement of 1559?
options: Elizabeth reunited England with the Pope to make peace with Spain.
A deliberate via media — a Protestant doctrine and English-language prayer book combined with some Catholic-style ceremony — designed to maximise conformity.
Elizabeth I personally commanded the English fleet at sea.
Elizabeth made England fully Protestant and banned Catholic worship outright.

mcqs.q: Why was the Spanish Armada defeated in 1588?
options: Elizabeth I personally commanded the English fleet at sea.
A combination of English tactics and fireships, poor Spanish planning, and the 'Protestant wind' storms that wrecked the fleet on the return.
Drake defeated the Armada single-handedly in a great sea battle.

options: Vesalius discovered the cause of disease and ended humoral theory.
Vesalius invented the microscope.
His 1543 De Humani Corporis Fabrica corrected Galen's errors via human dissection and accurate illustration, founding modern anatomy though not curing disease.
